turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. I do apologize for coming in late. The parking structure was packed, and I drove around for quite a while.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Uh, hang on. Sorry, what was that? This screen just froze on me.
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): I was only apologizing for my lateness, doctor. The lot was very crowded.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. You're here. Err, what brings you in? One sec, it keeps spinning.
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Of course. I have come in because of a lump in my groin.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): A lump. Say that once more? The beep cut you off.
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): A lump, on the right side of my groin. I notice it when I am lifting at work.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. And what does it do after that?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): It appears when I lift something heavy, and it goes away if I lie down. I would have said three months, no, it is six weeks. I misspoke.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Six weeks. Okay. Does it hurt?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): There is a mild ache by the evening. It is not severe.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting with it?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No, doctor. I have not vomited.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): No. I have not had a fever.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your weight. Have you lost any?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. I could not say with any certainty.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the chart jumped. Umm, any cough?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): No cough. My breathing has been quite normal.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): What do you do for work? I didn't catch it earlier.
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): I am a warehouse laborer, doctor. Manual work, lifting boxes, eight to ten hours on most days.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Are you taking anything for that ache?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes. Ibuprophen, four hundred milligrams, pardon me, that is wrong. Two hundred milligrams, by mouth, twice a day, for the past two weeks.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Two hundred, twice a day. Uh, lie back, I need to feel that side. Yeah, there's a soft bulge in the right groin, and it slips back when you lie flat.
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes, that is exactly what I notice at home.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): This is probably an inguinal hernia. That's my working impression. I wouldn't call it certain until surgery sees you.
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): I understand. Would that mean an operation?
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm referring you to general surgery, and they'll set the visit. Meanwhile, ease off the heavy lifting. If you must lift, keep it light and use your legs.
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. I will ask my supervisor about lighter duties.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sure. Reception will send the referral. Take care.

physical_examination.finding: Soft bulge that slips back when lying flat

clinical_assessment.basis: Working impression of a reducible groin lump, not certain until surgical review

clinical_actions.description: Ease off heavy lifting; if lifting, keep it light and use the legs

spec.situation: Manual worker with a groin lump that appears on lifting and goes away lying down; mild ache by evening; no vomiting; surgical referral planned, advice on lifting.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

omissions.text: Patient denied shortness of breath / said breathing has been quite normal.
Doctor discussed that surgery would evaluate the lump and that the diagnosis of inguinal hernia was not certain until surgery sees the patient.
Follow-up/coordination plan: reception will send the general surgery referral and they will set the visit.
